audit_result.proof_trace: `credentials: true` is hardcoded (line 29) while `origin` falls back to `'*'` when `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is unset (lines 24-26), directly violating the assertion. The `cors` npm package emits both `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` simultaneously — an invalid combination per CORS spec — and no startup guard or env validation prevents this default-insecure state. The `.env.example` comment explicitly documents wildcard as the fallback ('未設定の場合は全て許可'), confirming this is the default production behavior when `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is omitted.
audit_result.attack_scenario: When deployed without `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` set, any cross-origin page can read responses from unauthenticated endpoints (e.g., `/health` leaking Discord guild ID, bot user tag, WebSocket status) without restriction; additionally, non-browser clients (embedded WebViews, server-side SSRF proxies) are not bound by browser CORS enforcement and can make credentialed cross-origin requests to all API endpoints.

PROP-stem-bot-v21-inv-004.text: CORS origin must not default to wildcard '*' when credentials are enabled.
